intro: Myself, yourself, themselves… show that the subject does something to itself, or they add emphasis. English uses them much less than many other languages: “I get up, I remember, they meet” have no reflexive pronoun. This lesson shows when to use them… and when not to.
objectifs: Know the eight reflexive pronouns and their spelling (-self in the singular, -selves in the plural).
Use them when the subject and the object are the same person (hurt yourself, enjoy yourselves).
Use myself for emphasis (I made it myself) and by myself for “alone”.
Avoid reflexives with verbs like get up, relax, remember, meet, and tell themselves and each other apart.

texte: In the singular, add -self; in the plural, -selves. Be careful: “yourself” is for one person, “yourselves” for more than one.
Most forms use the possessive adjective (my, your, our), but him, it and them use the object pronoun: himself, itself, themselves. “Hisself” and “theirselves” are not standard English.

sections.titre: Use 1: the subject does the action to itself
texte: Use a reflexive pronoun when the subject and the object are the same person: She looked at herself in the mirror. Without the reflexive, the meaning changes: She looked at her (another woman).

Very common expressions: hurt yourself, cut yourself, burn yourself, introduce yourself, enjoy yourself (have a good time), help yourself (take food or drink freely), look after yourself, teach yourself, behave yourself.
“Enjoy” needs an object: I enjoyed the party or I enjoyed myself, but never “I enjoyed” alone.
exemples: Let me introduce myself: I'm Dr Ekotto.
Did you enjoy yourselves at the wedding?
Please help yourself to some cake.

texte: A reflexive pronoun can also add emphasis: “I did it, not another person”. Put it after the object or just after the subject: I painted the room myself. The manager himself called me.
“By + reflexive” means “alone, without help or company”: She lives by herself. I did it by myself. Synonyms: on my own, alone.
exemples: Did you make this cake yourself? — Yes, I did!
My grandmother still lives by herself.
The children went to school by themselves.

texte: Many verbs that are reflexive in other languages are NOT reflexive in English. Adding “myself” is a very common mistake.
For daily actions (wash, shave, dress), we normally add nothing: I wash and get dressed. The reflexive is possible only to show that it is difficult: The baby can dress himself now.

lignes: be anxious, say you are unhappy
marry, see for the first time

exemples: I usually get up at six and have a shower.

texte: “Themselves” means each person does the action to himself or herself. “Each other” (or “one another”) means the people do the action to the other person: it is reciprocal.
Compare: They're looking at themselves (each one in the mirror) / They're looking at each other (one looks at the other). We love each other.
exemples: Anna and Marc met in 2019. They call each other every day.
Anna calls Marc and Marc calls Anna.
The players were proud of themselves.
Each player was proud of his or her own work.

formule: myself · yourself · himself · herself · itself · ourselves · yourselves · themselves · by myself = alone · each other = one another
prononciation: “-selves” ends in /lvz/: say the v clearly.
For emphasis (I did it myself), the reflexive pronoun is strongly stressed at the end of the sentence.
“each other” joins: /iːtʃ ˈʌðə/, with the /ð/ sound of “the”.
erreurs: I get up myself at seven.
We enjoyed ourselves a lot. / We had a great time.
They love themselves. (meaning: one loves the other)
She lives by herself. / She lives on her own.
By + reflexive, or on + possessive + own.
You can help yourselves. (to one person)
One person: yourself; more than one: yourselves.

dialogue.contexte: At a birthday party in a garden in Lyon, the host welcomes his guests.
lignes: Welcome, everyone! Help yourselves to drinks and food.
Thanks, Julien. Wow, did you make all this yourself?
Most of it. My sister made the cake. She taught herself to bake last year.
Impressive! Oh, I don't know these people. Who are they?
Colleagues of mine. Go and introduce yourself, they're very nice.
OK. Careful with the barbecue, by the way. Don't burn yourself!
Don't worry. Just relax and enjoy yourself!
No reflexive with worry and relax; enjoy yourself.
I will. Look, the kids are playing by themselves in the garden. So cute!

mots: tell someone your name for the first time
take food or drink without asking
Can you do it by yourself?
She looked at herself in the mirror.
a glass in which you can see yourself
happy about something good you did

exercices.consigne: Complete with a reflexive pronoun or Ø (nothing).
items: I get up ___ at seven every day.
Marie and Paul write to (themselves / each other) every week.
The children dressed (themselves / each other) without help.
My brother and I don't see (ourselves / each other) very often.
The team was proud of (itself / each other).

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Correct it.
items: I wake myself up at six.
We enjoyed ourselves at the concert. / We enjoyed the concert.

exercices.consigne: Write one sentence for each situation.
items: You tell your guests to take the food freely.
Nobody helped you to make the cake.
I did it myself. / I made it myself.
Your aunt has no husband or children at home.
She lives by herself. / She lives alone. / She lives on her own.
Tom loves Ana and Ana loves Tom.
They love each other very much.

exercices.consigne: Write four sentences: something you did yourself, something you do alone, some advice for a friend (look after / enjoy yourself), and a sentence with each other.
items: I painted my living room myself last summer. I usually go running by myself. Look after yourself and don't work too much! My best friend and I call each other every Sunday.

a_retenir: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves.
Subject = object: hurt yourself, introduce myself, enjoy yourselves, help yourself.
Emphasis: I did it myself; alone: by myself / on my own.
No reflexive: get up, wake up, relax, remember, feel, hurry, worry, meet, sit down.
Reciprocal (one another): each other, not themselves.
